name: MG Road
blurb: The old spine of the city: metro, bookshops, Cubbon Park at one end and Church Street at the other.

name: Church Street
blurb: Bookshops, coffee and pubs on the city's most sociable street. Best after 5pm.

name: Brigade Road
blurb: A people-watching strip that still feels like old Bangalore on a Sunday evening.

name: Commercial Street
blurb: Bengaluru's old shopping street: sari shops, bakeries, street corners and a lot of noise.

name: Cubbon Park
blurb: The green heart of the city, ringed by museums, red-brick institutions and metro stops.

name: Shivajinagar
blurb: Dense, historic and full of character: Russell Market, the basilica and some of the city's best biryani.

name: Richmond Town
blurb: Quiet colonial-era streets, garden restaurants and a short walk to Cubbon Park.

name: Frazer Town
blurb: Bungalow-lined streets, old bakeries and some of the city's best biryani.

name: Cox Town
blurb: A leafy cantonment neighbourhood with old houses, quiet cafes and a village feel.

name: Cooke Town
blurb: Tree-lined streets and a slow, residential pace just east of Frazer Town.

name: Benson Town
blurb: A cantonment grid of old bungalows, churches and a handful of good neighbourhood cafes.

name: Vasanth Nagar
blurb: Between the race course and the palace: wide roads, old institutions and a central location.

name: Majestic
blurb: The city's transport heart: metro, rail and bus under one impossibly busy roof.

name: Chickpet
blurb: The old trading quarter for gold, silk and wholesale everything. Go with time to wander.

name: Basavanagudi
blurb: Old Bengaluru at its most delicious: temples, tiffin rooms and the Gandhi Bazaar din.

name: Malleshwaram
blurb: An unhurried grid of tiffin institutions, temples and the Sankey Tank loop.

name: Rajajinagar
blurb: A big, lived-in west Bengaluru neighbourhood with markets, temples and family restaurants.

name: Yeshwantpur
blurb: A major rail and metro junction in the northwest, with old markets and new towers.

name: Mathikere
blurb: Student country near IISc and New BEL Road: cheap eats, bookshops and a young crowd.

name: Hebbal
blurb: The northern gateway, with a lake, a flyover and a burst of new restaurants.

name: Yelahanka
blurb: A former town in the north, now a fast-growing edge of the city with old lakes and new layouts.

name: Jakkur
blurb: A restored lake and wetland in the north, good for birds and an early walk.

name: Hennur
blurb: A northeastern neighbourhood with big brewpub energy and a slower residential core.

name: Kalyan Nagar
blurb: A friendly northeast neighbourhood with a strong cafe and restaurant scene on 80 Feet Road.

name: Kammanahalli
blurb: A dense, cosmopolitan food pocket with everything from shawarma to filter coffee.

name: Banaswadi
blurb: Wide roads, old gardens and a growing cluster of cafes in the northeast.

name: Indiranagar
blurb: Cafe grids, boutiques and a metro stop. Start at 100 Feet Road, then get lost.

name: Domlur
blurb: An old-layout neighbourhood between the centre and the ORR, with quiet cafes and a cultural centre.

name: Koramangala
blurb: The city's original startup quarter, now a dense mix of cafes, pubs, bookshops and good bakeries.

name: HSR Layout
blurb: A newer neighbourhood with a serious cafe and restaurant strip on 27th Main.

name: BTM Layout
blurb: A busy south Bengaluru grid with markets, tiffin rooms and a young working crowd.

name: Jayanagar
blurb: A settled south-Bengaluru grid of markets, tiffin rooms and excellent filter coffee.

name: JP Nagar
blurb: A green, spread-out southern neighbourhood with lakes, theatres and good neighbourhood restaurants.

name: Banashankari
blurb: A temple-centred south Bengaluru area with old markets and a strong local food scene.

name: Vijayanagar
blurb: A west Bengaluru grid with metro access, markets and family-run restaurants.

name: Rajarajeshwari Nagar
blurb: A large western suburb around the Rajarajeshwari temple, with lakes and a growing food scene.

name: Kengeri
blurb: The western edge of the metro, with a university campus and a surprisingly good lake.

name: Whitefield
blurb: A tech suburb with its own coffee scene, brewpubs and a metro line to the centre.

name: Brookefield
blurb: A leafy east Bengaluru pocket with cafes, apartment blocks and a village-ish centre.

name: Marathahalli
blurb: The ORR's busiest stretch: malls, offices and a huge choice of everyday restaurants.

name: Bellandur
blurb: A lake-and-office district with a young crowd and a growing cafe scene.

name: Sarjapur Road
blurb: A long southeastern artery of apartments, schools and neighbourhood restaurants.

name: Electronic City
blurb: The southern tech belt, with its own metro line, food courts and pockets of quiet.

name: Bommanahalli
blurb: A busy southern junction with markets, old temples and a lot of everyday Bengaluru.

name: Ulsoor
blurb: A lake, an old temple and a grid of quiet streets just east of the centre.

name: Sadashivanagar
blurb: Grand old houses, wide leafy roads and a handful of understated cafes.

name: Sanjaynagar
blurb: A north Bengaluru neighbourhood with a strong local food scene and easy access to Hebbal.

name: RT Nagar
blurb: A central-north grid with markets, family restaurants and a quick route to the airport road.

name: New BEL Road
blurb: Student central: cheap eats, bookshops and a young crowd around IISc and BEL.

name: Kanakapura Road
blurb: A southern corridor of lakes, temples and new layouts, with the metro creeping south.

name: Bannerghatta Road
blurb: The road to the national park, with colleges, hospitals and a string of neighbourhood restaurants.

name: Old Airport Road
blurb: A central-east artery with hotels, malls and some of the city's oldest garden restaurants.

name: Hesaraghatta
blurb: Grasslands, a lake and a horizon that doesn't feel like Bengaluru.
